analyticalQuestion: Can nonnegative scalar-filtered vorticity covariances across scales, centers, or times provide a universal positive three-dimensional frame?

chartContract.family: normalized spectrum comparison, two-axis parameter curves, whole-space asymptotic trend, and aggregation comparison
chartContract.nonColorEncoding: hatching; solid, dashed, dotted, or dash-dot strokes; open or filled circle, square, triangle, or diamond markers; direct labels; and neutral references
chartContract.outputFootprint: double-column 178 by 126 millimetres with PDF, SVG, and 600 dpi PNG
chartContract.takeaway: scale count cannot create missing target-space directions; positive frames require quantitative nonparallel content

claimBoundary: Exact PDE witnesses and analytic frame identities; not DNS, not a failure of conditional or augmented frames, not a low-rank regularity theorem, and not a blow-up or Millennium result.

computation.configuration: three exact normalized spectra, four exact two-axis angle families over 99 rational energy fractions, 100 exact whole-space Gaussian quotients, and sixteen positive aggregation counts
computation.precision: SymPy exact rational and algebraic arithmetic; IEEE binary64 conversion only for plotting
computation.solver: closed covariance eigenvalue and Gaussian-moment formulas; no PDE time stepping

data.schema: panel, row role, series, exact x, exact value, numeric presentation value, and context
exact algebraic checks, output diagnostics, visual-QA declarations, and claim boundary

supportedClaim: Nonnegative scalar/componentwise scale, center, and time sums cannot remove a common vorticity nullspace. Exact shear and one-axis helical NSE solutions disprove a universal positive frame, while two nonparallel observed axes give a conditional positive control and full-rank whole-space data have no uniform constant.
